Novyy Bykiv Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernihivska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. The earliest evidence of a Jewish community in Novyy Bykiv dates to the first half of the 19th century, growing to 367 people (13.9 percent) by 1897, supported by two synagogues; by 1913, Jews owned both grocery shops, both local factories, and the only tobacco shop. Only 24 Jews remained by the 1926 census. This cemetery's establishment date is unknown, though epigraphic data suggests it already existed in the first half of the 20th century; its last known Hasidic burial took place in 1941, after which its stones were removed for use in road construction and other building projects. No mass graves are known to exist on the site.
